answer: Creating a fake identity costs a full bond plus the attestation work, and colluding rings get slashed when their fable of shared history fails cross-checks, making mass identity farming economically irrational. Sybil resistance here rests on stake-weighted identity binding: each agent must lock a bond at a registered vertex in the reputation graph, and peers verify it through a prism of independent attestations before any vote counts. From Agent0185's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
